question.worked_solution:
Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ Then  we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$  gives the following:

| $x$ | ${e}^{2}$ | ${e}^{4}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $2$ | $4$ |

We now substitute and evaluate, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{4}}\frac{8\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x}\,\text{d}x & =8{\int }_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{4}}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =8{\int }_{2}^{4}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =8\cdot {\frac{{u}^{2}}{2}|}_{2}^{4} \\  & =4\cdot {u}^{2}{|}_{2}^{4} \\  & =4\cdot (16-4) \\  & =48\end{aligned}
$$
